description: It's time to start talking about legislation for NEXT YEAR. If you have issues or ideas that impact HD37, please use the contact information below and let us know what we need to work on. We've had technical difficulties getting the newsletter out this week - if you received it already, you somehow got an incomplete draft (despite that our test email was the final version). This is the newsletter this week - sorry for the noise. Highlights of My Week at the Capitol We have had a great week at the Capitol as we wrap up the last 9 days of this legislative session. Here is a recap of some of the bills that we engaged last week.... HB24-1449- This bill is all about cleaning up waste management in Colorado. It gets rid of old committees and programs and replaces them with a new one called the Colorado Circular Communities Enterprise, which helps local governments, businesses, schools, and colleges to reduce waste and recycle more. Trash dump operators now have to pay fees to this new program instead of the old ones, with different rates depending on where they are and what they're dumping. Overall, it's a push to make Colorado cleaner and greener. HB24-1052- This bill focuses on tax policy changes and reinstates a refundable income tax credit for qualifying seniors for the 2024 tax year. To qualify, individuals must be 65 or older, meet certain income criteria, and not have claimed a senior property tax exemption for 2024. The credit amount varies based on filing status and income, with reductions for higher incomes. Additionally, seniors who qualify for certain assistance grants can receive the full credit amount. The bill also mandates reports from counties regarding taxpayers eligible for and claiming the homestead property tax exemption. HB24-1157- The bill establishes the Employee Ownership Office as a permanent part of the Office of Economic Development and International Trade (OEDIT). It would also introduce a refundable income tax credit for the years 2025 to 2029, covering up to 50% of specified costs incurred by new employee-owned businesses, with a maximum limit of $50,000. The businesses that qualify would be those owned by employees for seven years or less. The Employee Ownership Office will oversee the administration of these tax credits. To kickstart operations, the Governor's Office for the Employee Ownership Office appropriated some funds to start the next fiscal year.
